steps.intent: Our primary objective is to hold perpetrators accountable by establishing a robust, independent, and impartial attribution mechanism (UNIMI) following the horrific chemical attack in Douma, while ensuring immediate and unhindered access for the OPCW Fact-Finding Mission. The most difficult obstacle will be overcoming the Russian Federation's entrenched resistance and veto, as Moscow rejects any attribution mechanism that could implicate the Syrian regime and insists on Council oversight over findings. We anticipate strong backing from Western and allied partners, but bridging the divide with Russia without gutting the mechanism's independence will be virtually impossible.

messages.Bolivia (Plurinational State of): Bolivia categorically rejects the use of chemical weapons by anyone under any circumstances, but we cannot support a draft resolution that prejudges responsibility and seeks to establish a politicized mechanism without consensus. The priority of the Security Council must be to support the immediate and unhindered deployment of the OPCW Fact-Finding Mission to Douma to conduct an objective, on-site investigation. We warn against utilizing this Council to fabricate pretexts for unilateral military action, which would flagrantly violate the UN Charter and further destabilize Syria.
messages.China: China has consistently and unequivocally opposed the use of chemical weapons by any party, under any circumstances, and for any purpose. We support a comprehensive, objective, and impartial investigation into the reported incident in Douma by the OPCW Fact-Finding Mission, based strictly on science and verifiable facts rather than prejudged conclusions. Given the deep divisions among Council members, we urge the penholders to continue patient consultations in order to preserve Council unity and avoid forcing a vote on a divisive text.
messages.Côte d’Ivoire: Côte d’Ivoire reaffirms its categorical condemnation of any use of chemical weapons, which constitutes a flagrant violation of international law and international humanitarian law. We fully support the establishment of an independent, impartial, and professional investigative mechanism to identify the perpetrators of these heinous acts and ensure accountability. We encourage all members of the Council to demonstrate a spirit of compromise to preserve Council unity on this vital issue.
messages.Equatorial Guinea: Equatorial Guinea reiterates its unequivocal condemnation of any use of chemical weapons by any party, under any circumstances, as a grave violation of international law. We support the establishment of an independent, impartial, and professional mechanism to determine accountability, working in close cooperation with the OPCW Fact-Finding Mission. We urge the penholders and all Council members, especially the permanent members, to engage in constructive dialogue to achieve maximum consensus so that the Security Council can act with unity and resolve.
messages.Ethiopia: Ethiopia reiterates its principled and unequivocal condemnation of the use of chemical weapons by anyone, anywhere, and under any circumstances. We support the draft resolution and the urgent establishment of an independent, impartial, and professional investigative mechanism to determine accountability for the reported attack in Douma. We urge the penholders and all Council members to engage constructively and make every effort to bridge differences so that the Council can act with unity and speaking with one voice on this vital issue.
messages.Kazakhstan: Kazakhstan firmly condemns any use of chemical weapons, which constitutes a grave violation of international law, and reiterates its principled commitment to the global non-proliferation regime. We support the prompt establishment of an independent, impartial, and highly professional investigative mechanism to determine the facts and identify perpetrators. We urge all Council members, particularly the permanent members, to engage constructively and make every effort to find common ground so that the Security Council can act with unity on this critical issue.
messages.Kuwait: Kuwait expresses its strong support for this draft resolution and the urgent establishment of an independent, impartial, and professional mechanism to attribute responsibility for the horrific chemical attacks in Syria. The tragic events in Douma demand accountability, as any use of chemical weapons constitutes a flagrant violation of international law and Security Council resolutions. We call on all Council members to overcome divisions and unite behind this initiative to ensure justice for the victims.
messages.Netherlands: As a co-sponsor of this draft resolution, the Kingdom of the Netherlands fully supports the text as presented. Following the horrific chemical weapons attack in Douma, the Council must urgently re-establish an independent, impartial, and professional attribution mechanism to ensure that those responsible are held accountable. We urge all members of the Security Council to unite behind this text to uphold the international norm against the use of chemical weapons and support the vital work of the OPCW.
messages.Peru: As a co-sponsor of this draft resolution, Peru fully supports the text as drafted. We reiterate our principled and unwavering condemnation of any use of chemical weapons anywhere, by anyone, under any circumstances, which constitutes a grave violation of international law. It is imperative that the Security Council act decisively to establish an independent, impartial, and professional mechanism to identify perpetrators and combat impunity.
messages.Poland: As a co-sponsor of this draft resolution, Poland fully supports the text as drafted and urges its swift adoption. Following the horrific chemical attack in Douma, it is our legal and moral duty to ensure accountability and establish an independent, impartial mechanism to identify the perpetrators. We must send an unequivocal message that any use of chemical weapons will not be met with impunity.
messages.Russian Federation: This draft is fundamentally unacceptable as it prejudges the Douma incident prior to any professional verification and attempts to resurrect the discredited Joint Investigative Mechanism under a new guise. The immediate priority must be facilitating the swift deployment of the OPCW Fact-Finding Mission to Douma, not creating politicized attribution bodies to justify pre-planned aggression against a sovereign State. If the sponsors push ahead with this ultimatum-like text that disregards the basic tenets of the Chemical Weapons Convention and Syrian sovereignty, the Russian Federation will oppose it.
messages.Sweden: As a co-sponsor of this draft resolution, Sweden fully supports the text as drafted. The horrifying reports of chemical weapons use in Douma demand an urgent, principled, and united response from the Security Council. Establishing an independent, impartial, and professional mechanism to attribute responsibility and ensure accountability is essential to upholding international law and the global norm against chemical weapons.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom fully supports this draft resolution and is proud to co-sponsor it. Following the horrific chemical attack in Douma, the Council must act decisively to re-establish an independent, professional attribution mechanism and ensure full accountability. We urge all Council members to support this text without dilution or delay to uphold the global norm against the use of chemical weapons.
messages.United States of America: The United States fully supports this draft resolution as a co-sponsor and urges its immediate adoption without delay. Following the horrific chemical attack against innocent civilians in Douma, the Council must re-establish an independent, impartial, and professional attribution mechanism to hold perpetrators accountable. We will not accept any attempts to dilute the mechanism's independence or mandate, and we call on all Council members to support this vital text.

steps.summary: France added standard preambular language reaffirming Syria's sovereignty, independence, unity, and territorial integrity in constructive response to China. However, France firmly rejected all attempts by the Russian Federation and Bolivia to delete or subordinate the UNIMI attribution mechanism and dilute condemnations of the Douma chemical attack. The draft maintains a strong, robust 12-member coalition in favour of accountability.

steps.summary: France preserves the draft resolution without dilution to establish an independent, impartial, and professional mechanism (UNIMI) capable of attributing responsibility for chemical attacks in Syria, in particular the horrific attack in Douma. We reject demands from Russia and Bolivia that would dismantle independent attribution and subordinate investigations to political paralysis, standing firm alongside twelve Council members in defense of the international non-proliferation architecture.

before.Bolivia (Plurinational State of):
Bolivia categorically rejects the use of chemical weapons by anyone, anywhere, under any circumstances, as an unjustifiable and horrific violation of international law. However, we cannot support this draft resolution. 

First and foremost, this Council must not be used as an instrument to justify unilateral military actions or to bypass the foundational principles of the Charter of the United Nations. We are deeply alarmed by open threats of unilateral force made outside the framework of international law and this Council, which threaten to plunge the region into an even greater catastrophe. 

Furthermore, any credible mechanism must be genuinely independent, impartial, objective, and transparent. We must allow the experts of the Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons Fact-Finding Mission to deploy immediately to Douma, carry out a rigorous on-site investigation without preconditions or preconceived conclusions, and report their technical findings to the Council. Prejudging the facts and establishing a politicized mechanism undermines the search for the truth. For these reasons, Bolivia will vote against this draft resolution.
before.Russian Federation:
The draft resolution before us today is nothing more than a thinly veiled attempt to resurrect the discredited Joint Investigative Mechanism under a new guise, while prejudging the outcome of events in Douma and laying the groundwork for illegal military aggression against a sovereign State.

From the very beginning, Western delegations have not been interested in uncovering the truth. Before any investigation has even begun, the Syrian Government has already been publicly accused, convicted, and threatened with military strikes by Washington, London, and Paris. This draft resolution cynically seeks to endorse that false narrative. It describes the incident in Douma as an established chemical attack, completely ignoring that Russian military experts and medical personnel who visited the site found not a single trace of toxic chemicals, nor any patients showing symptoms of chemical poisoning in local hospitals. The so-called evidence consists entirely of fabricated footage produced by the notorious White Helmets—a terrorist-linked propaganda tool.

We proposed constructive, substantive amendments to ensure a genuinely impartial, objective, and professional investigation, adhering strictly to the standards of the Chemical Weapons Convention, including mandatory on-site visits and an unbroken chain of custody. All of our legitimate concerns were dismissed out of hand. The sponsors have deliberately chosen confrontation over consensus. 

Syria and Russia have already extended a formal invitation to the OPCW Fact-Finding Mission to visit Douma immediately, and full security guarantees have been provided. The inspectors must go to Douma and do their job without political pressure. Russia cannot and will not support a draft resolution that serves as a pretext for Western military adventurism and undermines the principles of international law. We will vote against it.
before.United States of America:
This resolution is the bare minimum that the Security Council can do to respond to the horrific attack in Douma. Over the weekend, the world watched in horror as pictures and videos emerged of innocent men, women, and children foaming at the mouth, suffocating, and dying in basements from what clearly appears to be a chemical weapons attack. 

For months, Russia protected the Assad regime by killing the Joint Investigative Mechanism. Today, we offer the Council a chance to re-establish an independent, impartial, and professional mechanism to determine attribution for chemical weapons use in Syria. This draft resolution before us gives the OPCW Fact-Finding Mission full and unfettered access, and it establishes a mechanism that is transparent, fair, and free from political interference. 

Russia’s own competing proposals are nothing more than a sham designed to shield Damascus and allow Russia to cherry-pick investigators and veto any findings it dislikes. The resolution we are voting on today represents a principled, objective standard. We urge all members of the Council to vote in favour of this text and take a stand against the barbaric use of chemical weapons.

after.China:
China is deeply concerned about the reports of the use of chemical weapons in Syria. China has always maintained a clear and consistent position on the issue of chemical weapons: we firmly oppose the use of chemical weapons by any State, organization, or individual, under any circumstances and for any purpose. Any use of chemical weapons, once proven, must be condemned, and the perpetrators must be held accountable. 

China supports an independent, comprehensive, objective, and impartial investigation into the reported incident of the use of chemical weapons in Douma, Syria. Such an investigation must be based on solid evidence, guided by scientific and professional standards, and lead to findings that can stand the test of time and history. We have taken note of the announcement by the Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons that it is deploying its Fact-Finding Mission to Syria to conduct an on-site investigation. We support the Fact-Finding Mission in carrying out its work in an objective, independent, and professional manner.

With regard to the draft resolution just put to the vote, Council members share the common goal of preventing the use of chemical weapons and bringing perpetrators to justice. However, there were major differences among members on specific elements of the draft resolution, including the mechanism’s mandate, working methods, and rules of engagement. Under such circumstances, members of the Security Council should have engaged in thorough, patient, and constructive consultations in order to bridge differences and seek the broadest possible consensus.

Forcing a vote while serious divisions remain will only lead to confrontation, undermine the unity of the Security Council, and fail to resolve the issue. Throughout the consultation process, China maintained an objective and fair position, actively called on the parties concerned to display flexibility, and worked tirelessly to preserve Council unity. Regrettably, our constructive proposals were not accepted, and the text was pushed to a vote despite significant differences. Based on this position, China abstained on the draft resolution.

China has always maintained that a political settlement is the only viable way out of the Syrian crisis. The sovereignty, independence, unity, and territorial integrity of Syria must be effectively respected. The Security Council must maintain its unity, support the United Nations as the main channel of mediation, and continue to push forward the political process in accordance with resolution 2254 (2015), so as to fundamentally alleviate the suffering of the Syrian people.
after.Ethiopia:
Ethiopia voted in favour of draft resolution S/2018/321.

Ethiopia’s principled position on the question of chemical weapons is consistent and clear. We believe that the use of chemical weapons by anyone, anywhere, under any circumstances is unacceptable and constitutes a grave violation of international law. Those responsible for the use of such horrific weapons must be identified and held accountable.

It is on the basis of this principled stance that we supported the draft resolution, which sought to establish an independent, impartial, and professional mechanism to identify the perpetrators of chemical attacks in the Syrian Arab Republic. We also attach the highest importance to the deployment and work of the Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons Fact-Finding Mission, and we stress the imperative need for all parties to provide the Mission with full, safe, and unhindered access to investigate the reported attack in Douma without delay.

We deeply regret that the Security Council has once again been unable to overcome its differences and speak with one voice on such a vital matter. The continued division within the Council does not serve the cause of peace, nor does it help alleviate the intolerable suffering of the Syrian people. We urge all Council members, particularly the permanent members, to exercise maximum restraint, avoid any escalation, and exert every effort to forge unity and consensus in addressing this grave crisis and in advancing a political solution in line with resolution 2254 (2015).
after.France:
France deeply regrets the result of the vote that has just taken place. By casting its veto once again—the twelfth time it has done so to protect the Syrian regime—Russia has chosen to plunge the Security Council into paralysis and to block the path towards truth and justice.

Last Saturday, 7 April, the world was confronted with unspeakable horror in Douma. Dozens of civilians, including women and children hiding in basements, were suffocated to death in what all available evidence indicates was a chemical attack. Such barbarity cannot be tolerated. The use of chemical weapons is an abomination, a flagrant violation of international law, and a direct threat to our collective security and the non-proliferation regime.

The draft resolution that was just put to the vote, and which received the broad support of twelve members of this Council, was both necessary and balanced. It sought to establish an independent, impartial, and professional mechanism to identify the perpetrators of chemical attacks in Syria, filling the vacuum left by the demise of the OPCW-United Nations Joint Investigative Mechanism. It also demanded full, unhindered, and safe access for the Fact-Finding Mission of the Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons. 

What is Russia afraid of? Why refuse an independent and objective inquiry if, as it claims, no chemical weapons were used or if the Syrian regime is blameless? By vetoing this text, Russia is not only shielding Damascus from accountability; it is undermining the non-proliferation regime that we have built over decades, and giving a free pass to the continued use of chemical weapons against innocent civilians.

France has consistently stated, at the highest level through the President of the Republic, Emmanuel Macron, that the use of chemical weapons constitutes an absolute red line. We will not allow the normalization of the use of these horrific weapons. Impunity is simply not an option.

Despite the paralysis imposed upon this Council by one of its permanent members, France will not abandon its responsibilities. We will continue to work tirelessly with all our partners to establish the facts, ensure accountability, and bring an end to the impunity enjoyed by the perpetrators of these atrocities.
after.Netherlands:
The Kingdom of the Netherlands deeply regrets that the Security Council was once again unable to unite and act today, due to the veto cast by the Russian Federation. 

We co-sponsored and voted in favour of the draft resolution because the use of chemical weapons is a flagrant violation of international law, international humanitarian law, and the Chemical Weapons Convention. Any use of chemical weapons, anywhere, at any time, by anyone, and under any circumstances, is unacceptable and constitutes a threat to international peace and security. Those responsible must be held accountable. Impunity cannot and must not be tolerated.

The images and reports from Douma over the weekend of innocent civilians—children, women, and men—suffocating to death in basements are horrifying. The international community owes it to the victims and their families to uncover the truth and ensure justice. 

Draft resolution S/2018/321 offered a balanced, objective, and credible path forward. It would have established an independent, impartial, and professional mechanism to identify the perpetrators of chemical attacks in Syria. It would have given the experts of the Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons (OPCW) Fact-Finding Mission the support and unhindered access they need to carry out their work.

By vetoing this draft resolution, the Russian Federation has chosen once again to shield perpetrators of chemical weapons attacks and to undermine the international non-proliferation architecture. A veto in this chamber cannot erase the facts, nor can it silence the victims. 

The Kingdom of the Netherlands reiterates its full support for the OPCW and its Fact-Finding Mission. We call on all parties, particularly the Syrian authorities, to grant the OPCW mission immediate, unconditional, and safe access to Douma and all relevant sites. We will continue to work tirelessly with our partners to uphold the international rules-based order, to ensure that the prohibition on chemical weapons is defended, and to ensure that there will be no impunity for these horrific crimes.
after.Peru:
Mr. President,

Peru co-sponsored and voted in favour of the draft resolution before us today in keeping with our firm and principled commitment to the defence of international law, international humanitarian law, and the fight against impunity.

Peru categorically condemns the use of chemical weapons by any party, anywhere, at any time, and under any circumstances. Such acts constitute grave violations of international law, war crimes, and threats to international peace and security. We express our profound sorrow and solidarity with the victims of the heinous attack in Douma on 7 April, which claimed the lives of dozens of civilians, including women and children.

We deeply regret that the Security Council has once again failed to act and that the use of the veto has prevented the adoption of this resolution. The Council had the responsibility to establish an independent, impartial, objective, and professional mechanism to determine the perpetrators, organizers, and sponsors of the use of toxic chemicals and chemical weapons in the Syrian Arab Republic, so as to ensure that those responsible are held accountable before justice.

Peru reiterates its full support for the Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons and welcomes the immediate deployment of its Fact-Finding Mission to Douma to clarify the facts on the ground. We demand that all parties guarantee the Mission full, safe, and unhindered access.

Finally, we emphasize the urgent need for the Security Council to overcome its divisions, act in unity to uphold international norms, and work collectively towards a peaceful, negotiated political solution to the conflict in Syria, in accordance with resolution 2254 (2015) and the Geneva Communiqué.

I thank you, Mr. President.
after.Poland:
Poland voted in favour of the draft resolution and co-sponsored it, and we deeply regret that the Security Council was once again unable to adopt it due to the veto cast by a permanent member.

Poland condemns in the strongest possible terms the reported use of chemical weapons in Douma on 7 April, which resulted in the tragic deaths and injuries of scores of innocent civilians, including many women and children. The images and reports emerging from Douma are truly horrific and shocking. 

We reiterate our principled and steadfast position: the use of chemical weapons anywhere, at any time, by anyone, and under any circumstances is unacceptable, constitutes a flagrant violation of international law, including international humanitarian law, and poses a grave threat to international peace and security. There can be no impunity for such abhorrent crimes, and those responsible must be identified and held accountable.

Following the non-renewal of the mandate of the OPCW-United Nations Joint Investigative Mechanism last year, an accountability gap was created that desperately needed to be filled. The draft resolution put forward today provided a balanced, objective, and credible basis to establish a truly independent, impartial, and professional mechanism to attribute responsibility for chemical weapons attacks in Syria. It is deeply regrettable that the Council has failed to shoulder its responsibility.

Poland fully supports the deployment of the OPCW Fact-Finding Mission to investigate the incident in Douma. We urge the Syrian authorities and all parties on the ground to cooperate fully and provide the Fact-Finding Mission with immediate, safe, and unfettered access to the site and to all relevant individuals and information. 

As a country staunchly committed to the Chemical Weapons Convention and the global non-proliferation regime, Poland will continue to support all international efforts aimed at eliminating chemical weapons and ensuring accountability for their use.
after.Sweden:
Sweden voted in favour of the draft resolution just voted on, of which we were also a proud co-sponsor. We deeply regret that, once again, the Security Council was prevented by a veto from shouldering its responsibility to uphold international peace and security and ensure accountability for the horrific use of chemical weapons.

The reports and images emerging from Douma over the weekend are appalling. Dozens of civilians, including women and children sheltering in basements, were killed and hundreds more injured in what clearly appears to have been an abhorrent chemical attack. We condemn in the strongest possible terms any use of chemical weapons. Their use under any circumstances is a flagrant violation of international law, including international humanitarian law, and constitutes a threat to international peace and security.

Impunity for such heinous crimes can never be accepted. Those responsible must be identified and held accountable. Following the demise of the OPCW-United Nations Joint Investigative Mechanism late last year, there has been a critical gap in the international architecture to establish attribution for chemical attacks in Syria. The draft resolution we voted on today would have filled that gap by establishing an independent, impartial, objective, and professional mechanism to identify perpetrators. 

The Security Council had an opportunity and a duty today to send an unequivocal message that the international norm against chemical weapons will be defended and that impunity will not prevail. It is a matter of profound regret that the Council has failed to do so.

We reiterate our full confidence in and support for the Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons, and we welcome the planned deployment of its Fact-Finding Mission to Douma. We demand that all parties on the ground grant the Fact-Finding Mission immediate, safe, and unfettered access to conduct its investigation without any hindrance or delay.
after.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort:
This is a grave day for the Security Council and for the international community. Today, Russia has chosen once again to use its veto—for the twelfth time on Syria, and the sixth time to protect the Syrian regime’s use of chemical weapons. 

By vetoing this draft resolution, Russia has not only failed to uphold international peace and security as a permanent member of this Council; it has actively undermined the international non-proliferation architecture and the global ban on chemical weapons. Russia has chosen to shield its murderous client, the Assad regime, rather than protect innocent civilians and stand up for international law.

Over the weekend, the world watched in horror at the images coming out of Douma: families, children, and infants suffocating in basements, foaming at the mouth, victims of yet another abhorrent chemical weapons attack. These atrocities demand a clear, independent, and resolute international response. The draft resolution put forward today, supported by twelve members of this Council, provided a balanced, impartial, and credible mechanism—the United Nations Independent Mechanism of Investigation—to determine who was responsible for these heinous acts. It was designed to build upon the work of the OPCW Fact-Finding Mission with full independence, professionalism, and objectivity.

Yet Russia vetoed it. Why? Because Russia knows all too well what any independent and impartial investigation would find. Russia knows that the Assad regime has repeatedly used chemical weapons against its own people, as the previous OPCW-UN Joint Investigative Mechanism conclusively demonstrated before Russia killed it last November.

Russia has tried to divert attention, claiming that the attack in Douma was staged or that no chemical weapons were used at all. But its actions speak louder than words. If Russia truly believed that the Syrian regime was innocent, it would have welcomed an independent investigation. Instead, it has killed the mechanism that would establish the truth. 

The United Kingdom will not stand by and allow the use of chemical weapons to be normalized. The victims of Douma and all victims of chemical attacks in Syria deserve justice. Russia may have vetoed this draft resolution today, but it cannot veto the truth, and it cannot veto the determination of the international community to hold the perpetrators of these barbaric crimes to account.
